verses.greek: Ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ἐν προσωπολημψίαις ἔχετε τὴν πίστιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς δόξης;
verses.literal: Brothers of Mine not with partiality do hold the faith of the Lord of us Jesus Christ the of glory.
verses.dgt: My brothers and sisters, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with partiality.

verses.greek: ἐὰν γὰρ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν ἀνὴρ χρυσοδακτύλιος ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ, εἰσέλθῃ δὲ καὶ πτωχὸς ἐν ῥυπαρᾷ ἐσθῆτι,
verses.literal: If for shall come into assembly of you a man with a gold ring in apparel splendid may come in then also a poor man in shabby apparel
verses.dgt: For if a man with a gold ring and bright clothing enters your assembly, and a poor man in dirty clothing also enters,

verses.greek: ἐπιβλέψητε δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν φοροῦντα τὴν ἐσθῆτα τὴν λαμπρὰν καὶ εἴπητε· Σὺ κάθου ὧδε καλῶς, καὶ τῷ πτωχῷ εἴπητε· Σὺ στῆθι ἢ κάθου ἐκεῖ ὑπὸ τὸ ὑποπόδιόν μου,
verses.literal: you may look also upon the one wearing the apparel the splendid and may say You yourself do sit here honorably and to the poor may say You yourself do stand or do sit there under the footstool of mine
verses.dgt: and you pay attention to the one wearing the bright clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but to the poor person say, “You stand there,” or, “Sit down by my footstool,”

verses.greek: οὐ διεκρίθητε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐγένεσθε κριταὶ διαλογισμῶν πονηρῶν;
verses.literal: not were discriminated among yourselves and you have become judges with thoughts evil?
verses.dgt: have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?

verses.greek: ἀκούσατε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. οὐχ ὁ θεὸς ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πτωχοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ πλουσίους ἐν πίστει καὶ κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἧς ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν;
verses.literal: do listen brothers of mine beloved Not the God has chosen the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that He promised to those loving Him?
verses.dgt: Listen, my beloved brothers and sisters. Did God not choose those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that he promised to those who love him?

verses.greek: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠτιμάσατε τὸν πτωχόν. οὐχ οἱ πλούσιοι καταδυναστεύουσιν ὑμῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἕλκουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς κριτήρια;
verses.literal: You yourselves however dishonored the poor. Surely the rich are oppressing you and they themselves dragging you into court?
verses.dgt: But you dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and themselves drag you into courts?

verses.greek: οὐκ αὐτοὶ βλασφημοῦσιν τὸ καλὸν ὄνομα τὸ ἐπικληθὲν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς;
verses.literal: Surely they themselves are denigrating the good Name which having been called upon you?
verses.dgt: Do they not blaspheme the good name that was called over you?

verses.greek: Εἰ μέντοι νόμον τελεῖτε βασιλικὸν κατὰ τὴν γραφήν Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε·
verses.literal: If indeed the law you keep royal according to the Scripture You will love the neighbour of you as yourself well you are doing
verses.dgt: If indeed you fulfill the royal law according to Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.

verses.greek: εἰ δὲ προσωπολημπτεῖτε, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεσθε, ἐλεγχόμενοι ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου ὡς παραβάται.
verses.literal: If however you show partiality sin you are committing being convicted by the law as transgressors.
verses.dgt: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

verses.greek: ὅστις γὰρ ὅλον τὸν νόμον τηρήσῃ, πταίσῃ δὲ ἐν ἑνί, γέγονεν πάντων ἔνοχος.
verses.literal: Whoever for all the law may keep may stumble but in one point he has become of all guilty.
verses.dgt: For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become guilty of all.

verses.greek: ὁ γὰρ εἰπών· Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς εἶπεν καί· Μὴ φονεύσῃς· εἰ δὲ οὐ μοιχεύεις φονεύεις δέ, γέγονας παραβάτης νόμου.
verses.literal: The One for having said Not you may commit adultery said also Not you may murder. If however not you do commit adultery do commit murder however you have become a transgressor of the law.
verses.dgt: For the one who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.

verses.greek: οὕτως λαλεῖτε καὶ οὕτως ποιεῖτε ὡς διὰ νόμου ἐλευθερίας μέλλοντες κρίνεσθαι.
verses.literal: Thus do speak and so do act as through the law of freedom being about to be judged.
verses.dgt: So speak and so act as those who are going to be judged by the law of freedom.

verses.greek: ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος· κατακαυχᾶται ἔλεος κρίσεως.
verses.literal: the For judgment without mercy will be to the one not having shown mercy it triumphs over mercy judgment.
verses.dgt: For judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

verses.greek: Τί ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ; μὴ δύναται ἡ πίστις σῶσαι αὐτόν;
verses.literal: What is profit brothers of mine if faith shall say anyone to have works however not he may have? Surely not is able the faith to save him?
verses.dgt: What benefit is it, my brothers and sisters, if someone says they have faith but do not have works? Can that faith save them?

verses.greek: ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς,
verses.literal: Now if a brother or a sister without clothes shall be and lacking the of daily food
verses.dgt: If a brother or sister is without clothing and lacking daily food,

verses.greek: εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, τί ὄφελος;
verses.literal: may say then anyone to them out from you do go in peace do be warmed and do be filled surely not may give however to them the needful things for the body what is profit?
verses.dgt: and one of you says to them, “Go in peace, be warmed and be filled,” but you do not give them what is necessary for the body, what benefit is that?

verses.greek: οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις, ἐὰν μὴ ἔχῃ ἔργα, νεκρά ἐστιν καθʼ ἑαυτήν.
verses.literal: So also the faith only unless it shall have works then dead it is by itself.
verses.dgt: So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.

verses.greek: Ἀλλʼ ἐρεῖ τις· Σὺ πίστιν ἔχεις κἀγὼ ἔργα ἔχω. δεῖξόν μοι τὴν πίστιν σου χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων, κἀγώ σοι δείξω ἐκ τῶν ἔργων μου τὴν πίστιν.
verses.literal: But will say someone You yourself faith have and I myself works have do show me the faith of you without the works and I myself you will show by the works of mine the faith
verses.dgt: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have works.” Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

verses.greek: σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός; καλῶς ποιεῖς· καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν.
verses.literal: You yourself believe that one is the God Well you are doing! Even the demons believe that and shudder!
verses.dgt: You believe that God is one. You do well. Even the demons believe—and shudder.

verses.greek: θέλεις δὲ γνῶναι, ὦ ἄνθρωπε κενέ, ὅτι ἡ πίστις χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων ἀργή ἐστιν;
verses.literal: Do you want however to come to know O man foolish that the faith apart from the works worthless is?
verses.dgt: But do you want to know, empty person, that faith apart from works is useless?

verses.greek: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἀνενέγκας Ἰσαὰκ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον;
verses.literal: Abraham the father of us not by works was justified having offered Isaac the son of him upon the altar?
verses.dgt: Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered Isaac his son on the altar?

verses.greek: βλέπεις ὅτι ἡ πίστις συνήργει τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἡ πίστις ἐτελειώθη,
verses.literal: Do you see that the his faith was working with the works of him and by the his works the his faith was perfected?
verses.dgt: You see that faith was working together with his works, and by the works faith was brought to completion,

verses.greek: καὶ ἐπληρώθη ἡ γραφὴ ἡ λέγουσα· Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην, καὶ φίλος θεοῦ ἐκλήθη.
verses.literal: And was fulfilled the Scripture which is saying Believed then Abraham the in God and it was counted to him for righteousness and a friend of God he was called.
verses.dgt: and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.

verses.greek: ὁρᾶτε ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος καὶ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως μόνον.
verses.literal: You see that by works is justified a man and not by faith alone.
verses.dgt: You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.

verses.greek: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ὑποδεξαμένη τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἑτέρᾳ ὁδῷ ἐκβαλοῦσα;
verses.literal: Likewise then also Rahab the prostitute not by works was justified having received the messengers and by another way having sent them forth?
verses.dgt: And likewise, was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way?

verses.greek: ὥσπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα χωρὶς πνεύματος νεκρόν ἐστιν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις χωρὶς ἔργων νεκρά ἐστιν.
verses.literal: Just as for the body apart from spirit dead is so also the faith apart from works dead is.
verses.dgt: For just as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead.
